title: Reduce Metrics page warm-up delay
summary: Queue Metrics page refreshes reliably, preserve neutral Metrics state until a request fails, and avoid redundant parsing of unchanged Metrics history inputs.
reason: Opening Metrics during an in-flight automatic refresh drops the page request, startup renders a false unavailable state without requesting Metrics, and cold reads repeatedly parse large completed-history and sidecar-cache files.
behavior_before: Metrics navigation could wait for the next 15-second poll, show historical-only before any Metrics request, and repeatedly parse unchanged history/cache files.
behavior_after: Metrics navigation queues one page-scoped refresh, unavailable state requires an actual Metrics failure, and immutable manifest/cache-derived work is reused until its file fingerprint changes.
manual_validation: 81.68 MB completed-history benchmark: 0.3945s cold, 0.0001s unchanged warm
85 focused tests passed across Metrics, WebView static/navigation, and browser queue behavior
Final Node syntax, task-scoped Ruff, git diff whitespace, and packet schema checks passed
Generated summaries refreshed for 9 task-owned sources; second pass reported 9 unchanged
Independent correctness re-review passed with no remaining findings
Independent security/safety re-review passed with no remaining findings
Ruff passed on all task-owned Python files
rollback_plan: Revert the WebView refresh coordination and Metrics read-cache changes plus their focused regressions; no state, manifest, config, or media migration is required.
notes:
Python impact: read-only Metrics facade/source-cache behavior only. No media policy, source/scratch/output mutation, pending-publish drain, settings persistence, route schema, or public API contract changes. Representative real-media validation is not required.
Independent correctness and safety review findings were addressed with a dedicated history RLock, 60-second bounded revalidation, in-lock fingerprinting, preserved malformed-line counts, and executable in-flight navigation coverage.
Canonical release self-test ran for 556 seconds. Task-relevant layout/schema/environment/Tauri checks passed; the overall gate remained red on unrelated pre-existing audit-doc, package-cycle, Ruff, release-inventory, and WebView reliability baseline findings in the dirty worktree.
